key_insight: Data-driven equation discovery can recover governing PDE structure for nonlinear liquid film flows, but identifiability becomes fragile when candidate terms are highly correlated and early-time transients dominate the residuals.
engineering_relevance: The work clarifies when physics discovery methods are trustworthy for thin-film flow modeling, helping engineers set realistic expectations for reduced-order modeling and model calibration.
method: Curated liquid-film flow data to create a best-case discovery setting.
Used expert-informed candidate equation libraries with monomial basis functions across multiple scales.
Tested identifiability under multi-collinearity and transient-rich dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that even with carefully curated data and expert knowledge, the discovery process still encountered multi-collinearity and large residuals during early-time transients.
watch_item: Monomial basis choices in multi-scale flow settings can create severe parameter non-uniqueness, so discovered equations may be unstable without stronger regularization or alternative bases.
paper_title: Data-Driven Equation Discovery for Nonlinear Liquid Film Flows
